title: Word frequency with normalization
prompt:
Count the words of the text given at the end. Rules:
- Convert the text to lowercase. A word candidate is a maximal run of the letters `a` to `z` and apostrophes (`'`); every other character (spaces, digits, punctuation, hyphens) separates candidates.
- Remove all apostrophes at the start and at the end of a candidate (`''curious` becomes `curious`; an apostrophe inside, as in `don't`, stays).
- Then ignore the candidate if it has fewer than 3 characters (an inner apostrophe counts as a character), or if it is one of these stop words: the, and, for, are, but, not, you, all, any, can, had, her, was, one, our, out, his, has. Every other candidate is a word.
Print the 8 most frequent words, the most frequent first; words with the same count are ordered by plain character order, in which `'` comes before every letter. Each of these lines is the word, then dots, then the count, with as many dots as make the line exactly 24 characters long (for example `cat....................7`). Then print `distinct: N`, the number of different words, and `longest: W`, the longest word (if several words share the greatest length, the first of them in plain character order).
The text (between the backticks): `The rabbit's hole was deep; the rabbit didn't stop. 'Down, down, down!' said Alice -- and down-hill she went, past rabbit-holes, shelves, maps and jars. Was it 3 o'clock? It wasn't: the clock said half-past 4. ''Curious,'' thought Alice, ''curiouser'' -- and the rabbit's watch said nothing at all. DOWN went the jars, down went the maps; Alice didn't mind, didn't care, didn't stop. The rabbit's ears twitched; the rabbit whispered.`
